*Generated by `php artisan agrivisit:tools --json`, from the same schemas the gate
validates against and from which the model's function declarations are built.
There is no second copy, so the catalogue cannot drift from the system's
behaviour.*

---

## 1. The catalogue

| Tool | Access | Approval | Required parameters | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **`farm_profile_lookup`** | read | no | `farm_id` | Look up a farm by its ID to get its district, crops, last visit date, outstanding issues and previous advice. |
| **`schedule_visit`** | write | yes | `farm_id`, `visit_date`, `purpose` | Schedule a field visit to a farm on a given date. The officer must approve before it is booked. |
| **`log_followup`** | write | yes | `farm_id`, `visit_id`, `notes`, `outcome` | Record a follow-up note and outcome against an existing visit. The officer must approve before it is saved. |

Two further tools, `faulty_probe` and `malformed_probe`, exist solely to exercise
failure paths. They are disabled by default, never declared to the model, and are
described in the failure evidence document as test instrumentation rather than
product capability.

## 2. Input schemas

| Tool | Parameter | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| **`farm_profile_lookup`** | `farm_id` | string | Required. Pattern `^UG-[A-Z]{3}-\d{3}$`. The farm must exist, or `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`. |
| **`schedule_visit`** | `farm_id` | string | Required. Same pattern. The farm must exist. |
| | `visit_date` | string (date) | Required. `YYYY-MM-DD`, a real calendar date, today or later in the application timezone. |
| | `purpose` | string | Required. 1 to 200 characters. |
| **`log_followup`** | `farm_id` | string | Required. Same pattern. Must match the visit's farm. |
| | `visit_id` | string | Required. Pattern `^V-\d{4,}$`. The visit must exist. |
| | `notes` | string | Required. 1 to 2000 characters. |
| | `outcome` | string (enum) | Required. One of `resolved`, `ongoing`, `escalated`. |

Any property not listed is rejected as `INVALID_ARGUMENTS`. The schema is a closed
set, which stops an extra field being smuggled through and keeps a tool and its
declaration from drifting apart.

## 3. Output schemas

| Tool | Fields | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **`farm_profile_lookup`** | `farm_id`, `district`, `crops`, `last_visit`, `outstanding_issues`, `previous_advice` | object | Only the declared fields are returned; the farm record's other fields are projected away. |
| **`schedule_visit`** | `visit_id`, `farm_id`, `visit_date`, `status` | object | `visit_id` is `V-0000` upward. `status` is always `scheduled` on creation. |
| **`log_followup`** | `entry_id`, `farm_id`, `recorded_at` | object | `entry_id` is `F-0000` upward. `recorded_at` is ISO 8601. |

Output is validated too. A tool returning anything that does not match its own
schema fails with `UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE` and the data is discarded. A wrong-shaped
answer is a failure, not a partial success.

## 4. Authorization and failure behaviour

| Code | When it is returned |
|---|---|
| **`TOOL_NOT_FOUND`** | The requested name is not registered. Logged, because an unlisted call is the condition Week 1 Story 11 is about. |
| **`INVALID_ARGUMENTS`** | Arguments failed the input schema, or a business rule such as a past visit date. Every error is reported, not just the first. |
| **`UNAUTHORIZED`** | The tool is registered but not in the enabled list. |
| **`APPROVAL_REQUIRED`** | A write tool was called without approval. Nothing executes; the pending call is returned for replay. |
| **`RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`** | The tool's subject does not exist. |
| **`SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`** | A dependency the tool needs could not be reached. Any exception is caught and converted; a tool never takes down the request. |
| **`UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE`** | The tool returned data failing its own output schema. |

## 5. How declarations reach the model

Gemini's function declarations accept an OpenAPI subset and reject `pattern`,
`minLength`, `maxLength`, `minimum`, `maximum`, `format` and union types. These are
not dropped: each is folded into the property's description, so the model is still
told the rule even though the API cannot express it.

| Dropped keyword | Appended to the description |
|---|---|
| **`pattern ^UG-[A-Z]{3}-\d{3}$`** | Format: UG-XXX-000 (X = capital letter, 0 = digit). |
| **`format: date`** | Format: YYYY-MM-DD. |
| **`maxLength: 200`** | Maximum 200 characters. |
| **`minLength: 1`** | Must not be empty. |

A model told the rule produces valid arguments most of the time. A model not told
produces invalid ones, and the failure appears to be the model's fault when it is
the declaration's.

> **Single source**
>
> The catalogue, the runtime validation and the model's declarations are all
> generated from one schema per tool. A test asserts that every declaration
> contains no unsupported keyword at any depth, and that each tool's `required`
> list names only properties the schema defines.
